questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] What is the big red spot on Jupiter?
A. A mountain
B. A red desert
C. A giant storm
Answer: C. The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is a massive storm, much like a hurricane, but significantly larger. It’s been raging for at least 300 years, observed since the 1600s. The storm is so large that the Earth could fit inside it.
questions.de: Was für ein Gebilde ist der Große Rote Fleck auf dem Jupiter?
questions.en: What kind of feature is Jupiter's Great Red Spot?

timeline.labelEn: The present Great Red Spot on Jupiter is probably first seen; it has been studied continuously since
timeline.labelDe: Der heutige Große Rote Fleck auf dem Jupiter wird vermutlich erstmals gesichtet; seither wird er durchgehend beobachtet

questions.notes: Card's 'observed since the 1600s / at least 300 years' is uncertain: a spot was seen 1665–1713, but a 2024 study suggests it differs from today's spot, observed since 1831. It is the Solar System's largest anticyclonic storm.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] How do hippos move underwater?
A. By swimming with their legs
B. By floating and paddling
C. By walking and bounding
Answer: C. Hippos move underwater by walking or bounding along the bottom of rivers and lakes. They push off surfaces to propel themselves forward, rather than swimming in the traditional sense.
questions.de: Flusspferde schwimmen kaum — wie bewegen sie sich stattdessen unter Wasser fort?
questions.en: Hippos hardly swim at all — how do they move underwater instead?
questions.answerDe: Indem sie über den Grund laufen oder hüpfen
questions.answerEn: By walking or bounding along the bottom

timeline.labelEn: Carl Linnaeus scientifically describes the common hippopotamus, Hippopotamus amphibius
timeline.labelDe: Carl von Linné beschreibt das Flusspferd, Hippopotamus amphibius, wissenschaftlich
